600.author: eshaoliu
600.body:
## Problem

Issue #589 reports two opaque `run_python` failures before the model finds the lmfit 1.3.4 `conf_interval` calling convention. The issue did not include the original exception text. Direct reproduction against lmfit 1.3.4 confirms the likely failures:

- `lmfit.conf_interval(result)` → `TypeError: conf_interval() missing 1 required positional argument: 'result'`
- `lmfit.conf_interval(result.minimizer, result)` on a `ModelResult` → `AttributeError: 'ModelResult' object has no attribute 'minimizer'`
- `MinimizerResult.conf_interval()` → `AttributeError: 'MinimizerResult' object has no attribute 'conf_interval'`

The valid forms are `ModelResult.conf_interval(...)` and `lmfit.conf_interval(minimizer, result)`.

## Changes

- `skills/code-engineer/SKILL.md`: adds a version-sensitive API section before the workflow. It gives the two valid lmfit 1.3.4 calls, names the invalid forms, requires an `errorbars` check, and points to the reference before the first call. The output-handling guidance now asks for the installed version and the exact exception instead of a guessed correction.
- `skills/code-engineer/references/lmfit-confidence-intervals.md`: documents the result-type matrix, the exact observed errors, and the `errorbars` failure condition.
- `skills/code-engineer/references/lmfit_confidence_intervals.py`: runnable Michaelis-Menten example covering both fit paths.

No exception is swallowed, and no successful result is fabricated. The executor and runtime error handling are unchanged.

## Validation

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.12.14, lmfit 1.3.4, numpy 2.2.6.

The reference example was run directly and through the bundled executor:

```text
lmfit version: 1.3.4
ModelResult vmax: 12.071
ModelResult vmax stderr: 0.091
ModelResult CI parameters: ['km', 'vmax']
MinimizerResult vmax: 12.071
MinimizerResult vmax stderr: 0.091
MinimizerResult CI parameters: ['km', 'vmax']
```

The invalid `lmfit.conf_interval(result)` path was also run through `skills/code-engineer/scripts/execute.py`. It still emits the real traceback and `TypeError`, with `Exit code: 1`, so the documented failure is not hidden.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED.** The agent/`run_python` timeline and local stack require Linux or macOS per `CONTRIBUTING.md`; this session is Windows 11. I executed the library-level example and the bundled executor path, but not the full product journey. The original session's exception text was unavailable, so the reproduction covers the candidate calling conventions rather than the exact transcript.

Partial fix; keep #589 open until the first-call guidance is verified through the agent/`run_python` path on a supported host.

Refs #589

## Release

Release category: release:fix
GitHub label: pending a maintainer; this contributor account has no upstream write access.
User impact: the code-engineer skill now steers the first lmfit confidence-interval call to the correct 1.3.4 signature and requires checking `errorbars`; failed calls still surface the real exception.
Compatibility and migration: none.
600.head: fix/code-engineer-lmfit-conf-interval-guidance
600.title: fix(code-engineer): steer lmfit confidence intervals to the 1.3.4 API

601.author: HongyeZhou
601.body:
## Summary
After #466, Reviewer defaults on and Specialists no longer flash off while loading, but the **composer Automatic review control** still treated unloaded system Reviewer settings (`undefined`) as capability-off. That produced a misleading “unavailable: Reviewer Specialist is off” title/Off label on the new Session path. This change mirrors the Specialists loading rule for the composer, and adds store/journey coverage for the residual #588 cases (new Session defaults under an existing Project; no false unavailable notice when Reviewer is on).

## What #466 already fixed
- Shared `DEFAULT_REVIEWER_*` / `DEFAULT_SESSION_REVIEWER_*` (on) for new catalogs/Sessions
- One-shot lift of pre-#353 persisted Reviewer-off catalogs
- Specialists UI loading flash (`undefined` vs `false`)

## Leftover gap fixed here
- Composer loading flash / false unavailable presentation while `getReviewerSpecialistSettings` is in flight
- Explicit S3 store coverage: new Session gets current Automatic review defaults without rewriting older Sessions’ saved `false`

## Validation (candidate `8602b669d`)
- Scenario UTs: `AutomaticReviewComposer` 4 passed; Reviewer/store cases including new “new Session under existing Project” passed
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4917 / executed 4917 / passed 4917 (full green on matching tree); tip re-run saw 1 unrelated CAS flake that passed 3/3 isolated retries
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 24 / executed 24 / passed 24
- Mocked journey `journey-reviewer-auto-audit`: **passed** (toggle On, no unavailable status when Reviewer on; one-click off + reload; manual Run review; unavailable only when Reviewer off)
- L3 real (`CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm ci:e2e:real -- --profile merge --backend legacy`): MiniMax returned **402** insufficient balance; DeepSeek `deepseek-chat` **planned 9 / executed 9 / passed 9**

## E2E user journeys
- Mocked: `test/journey-reviewer-auto-audit.spec.ts` — Automatic review available without false “Reviewer off” block; one-click off; manual review still works
- Real L3 merge profile: 9/9 passed (DeepSeek)

## Release
Release category: release:fix  
User impact: New/upgraded Sessions no longer briefly (or while settings load) look like Automatic review is blocked by a default-off Reviewer when policy says it should be available.  
Compatibility and migration: none beyond existing #466 catalog migration; intentional persisted `false` values remain unchanged.

Closes #588  
Related to #413
601.head: fix/588-auto-review-ui
601.title: fix(web): stop Automatic review composer flash after #466

602.author: zhaozhaozz
602.body:
PDFs dropped into the workspace currently remain raw files. This change sends PDFs identified by MIME type or file extension through the existing `papers/upload` pipeline, so extracted text, tables and provenance are available in the current session. CSV and other attachments keep the existing workspace upload path.

Fixes #333

## Changes

- Reuse `uploadPaper` for Drop files and file-picker PDFs; retain per-file errors and continue processing the rest of a mixed batch.
- Refresh the workspace after extraction, guard against applying upload results to another session, and update the English and Chinese drop hints.
- Extend paper-upload coverage to read extracted tables and execute the session agent's actual `read_file` tool against extracted text.
- Add a real-parser browser journey for PDF + CSV drag-and-drop, in-app protocol reading, CSV preview, MIME/extension detection and invalid-PDF recovery. The existing raw Artifact preview fixture now seeds its minimal PDF through the generic workspace API; its PDF preview assertions remain in place.

## Validation

Tested head: `34282896af3460ff53726962c582910db785860c`.

| Check | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Web UT: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` | 1060 | 1060 | 1060 | 0 / 0 |
| Paper and workspace-upload UT: `node --import tsx --test src/papers.test.ts src/workspace-upload.test.ts` in `services/api` | 12 | 12 | 12 | 0 / 0 |
| Paper-upload integration: `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='PDF upload extracts' src/server.test.ts` in `services/api` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Targeted browser journeys, command below | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| Architecture/script checks: `pnpm architecture:check` | 69 | 69 | 69 | 0 / 0 |

`pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, E2E metadata validation and `git diff --check` also passed. Architecture boundaries checked 295 package source files.

Local validation used the targeted checks above. Full `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st` and `ci:e2e` slices were not run locally: this task requested scoped verification, and the executor/adapter behavior is unchanged. Live-model layers were not run because this flow requires no model calls.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** — 3 planned, 3 executed, 3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped on the tested head above. Chromium used the isolated product Web/API with the real local paper worker; no real models or remote paper sources were used. The PDF journey ran at 1280 × 720, DPR 1.

Command, from the pinned `.e2e` environment with an isolated `E2E_BASE_URL` and `E2E_API_TOKEN`:

```sh
npm run test:mocked -- journey-drop-pdf.spec.ts journey-artifact-source-preview.spec.ts
```

| Scenario | Expected and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Drop PDF + CSV | One succeeded paper in the current session; only the PDF enters paper intake; CSV remains an ordinary attachment. |
| Read parsed protocol | In-app Markdown contains the extracted temperature, replicates, units and rate constant; CSV opens in the existing table viewer. |
| Invalid PDF + valid MIME-identified PDF + CSV | The invalid file reports failure; the next PDF is parsed and the CSV is saved. |
| Existing Artifact and workspace previews | Both existing browser journeys pass, including raw PDF and CSV previews. |
| Agent access, integration check | The actual session `read_file` tool returns the parsed scientific text. No full agent Run was invoked. |

![The dropped PDF's parsed protocol is readable in the current session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fa0ce13-7a82-4602-a5fb-ff2b45ae86a6)

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: Dropped PDFs are automatically parsed as papers and their extraction results are available to the user and session agent. Other attachments keep their current behavior. No migration is required.
602.head: fix/issue-333-drop-pdf-parse
602.title: fix(web): parse PDFs dropped into the workspace as papers

603.author: zhaozhaozz
603.body:
Parallel research agents already share arXiv concurrency/pacing, but later calls could still queue behind a known upstream failure and repeated 406 responses had no endpoint-health suppression. This change shares health and cooldown within one service process, bounds admission and actual attempts, and permits one recovery probe after cooldown.

Fixes #208

## Behavior

- Preserve existing concurrency and request intervals. Governed calls make one MCP attempt, so internal retries cannot bypass pacing while holding a slot. Missing queue limits now default to 8 waiters / 20 seconds, capped by the tool timeout.
- Share 429 cooldown by upstream group and effective endpoint/authentication digest, honoring Retry-After in seconds or HTTP-date. Without a hint, backoff starts at 1 second and caps at 30 seconds. Reject affected waiters immediately and return retry timing instead of independent sleeps.
- Keep request-specific or unattributed 406 local. Three distinct, consecutive, provider-attributed endpoint refusals within one minute trigger source/tool suppression: 30-second initial cooldown, capped at 120 seconds. Repeated identical inputs do not reach the threshold.
- Admit one post-cooldown probe; success restores access, failure continues bounded suppression, and cancellation releases the slot and probe permit. Credential changes remain isolated; other sources continue working.
- Return a short unavailable/blocked explanation plus structured timing, same-kind alternative source IDs and citation/evidence guidance. Never claim an uncalled alternative or unavailable content was retrieved. Sanitize provider metadata and diagnostics. No distributed state, infrastructure or new user controls.

## Validation

Tested candidate: `ae5f87f0608a008e9ced844d848621071077b983`.

| Check | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Affected Node UT and deterministic broker/transport fault injection | 117 | 117 | 117 | 0 / 0 |
| Bundled Python MCP tests, including HTTP failure attribution and Retry-After | 30 | 30 | 30 | 0 / 0 |
| Production API user journey | 5 | 5 | 5 | 0 / 0 |

Commands: `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm docs:check`, `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`, targeted `node --import tsx --test` for data-source, tool registry, public-biomed manifests and affected API MCP suites, and Python unittest discovery under `services/gateway/tests`.

Documentation validation: 172 files linted, 144 Markdown files link-checked. Static architecture boundaries: 297 package source files checked.

Baseline regression at `87a87dd36e404cdbc809761991e05e21aa911b8a`: after an injected 429, a later agent round returned a queue timeout without shared retry timing. The same regression passes with fail-fast shared cooldown and no additional upstream attempt.

An extra architecture-wrapper run passed 68/69 script tests; its unrelated RACE contract test could not initialize the default uv cache in the sandbox. The standalone architecture boundary checker passes. Full `ci:ut`, `ci:st` and mocked browser `ci:e2e` were not run: validation targets the changed backend and production API path. No real arXiv/PubMed, real models, DRB or Nightly evaluations were run.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** — `node test/api/source-health-journey.mjs`, production API process and official SDK HTTP MCP fixtures; no in-process API replacement or model calls. Tested SHA: `ae5f87f0608a008e9ced844d848621071077b983`.

| User scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configure isolated sources and two research sessions | Real API startup and usable local sources | PASS |
| Concurrent 429 and a later agent round | Shared cooldown and bounded return without amplification | PASS: 9 user calls produced 1 MCP attempt; persisted audit includes retry timing |
| Failed recovery probe, then upstream recovery | One probe during continued failure; later real results | PASS: one failed probe, then two successful accesses |
| Request-specific versus persistent endpoint 406 | Request errors remain local; sustained rejection suppresses later calls | PASS: 4 request-specific failures remain callable; 3 distinct endpoint refusals trigger suppression; later round makes 0 attempts |
| Credentials and healthy source isolation | New credentials can attempt; original cooldown persists; healthy source works | PASS: isolated attempt, preserved original cooldown and real healthy-source result; no credentials in audit |

The journey asserts the short unavailable-source explanation and honest blocked feedback. Broker fault injection additionally verifies queue exhaustion/timeouts, cancellation, probe cancellation, recovery with changed failure status, continued source pacing, available scholarly fallback and unchanged citation/full-text evidence boundaries.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: Parallel research avoids repeated waits and calls to a known failing source; diagnostics distinguish throttling and endpoint refusal while preserving evidence requirements.
Compatibility and migration: No user migration. Internal broker queue defaults are now bounded; generic ResourceRateLimiter optional dimensions remain available. State is process-local and resets on restart.
603.head: fix/issue-208-source-health
603.title: fix(data-source): share cooldown and bound recovery across research agents
